data.title: Ducommun: Vision 2032 Growth, Margin Expansion, and Undervalued Transformation Support Unchanged $201 Buy Target
data.description:
In a report released yesterday, Noah Poponak from Goldman Sachs maintained a Buy rating on Ducommun, with a price target of $201.00.

Noah Poponak has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors that highlight Ducommun’s long-term growth and profitability potential. He notes that management’s “Vision 2032” plan calls for robust organic revenue expansion in both defense and commercial aerospace, with particularly strong momentum in missile and radar programs, supported by a healthy demand backdrop and incremental contributions from future acquisitions.

He also emphasizes the company’s plan to meaningfully improve margins through a richer mix of engineered products, greater aftermarket exposure, operating leverage, and more disciplined pricing on long-term agreements. In addition, Ducommun’s role as an acquisition platform and its ongoing transformation are, in his view, not fully reflected in the current valuation, as the stock trades at a discount to the broader aerospace supply chain on forward EBITDA multiples, supporting his unchanged $201 price target and Buy recommendation.

data.title: INNIO Backlog Strength and Data Center Demand Support Buy Rating as Price Target Trimmed to $40
data.description:
Analyst Joe Ritchie from Goldman Sachs maintained a Buy rating on INNIO Holding GmbH and decreased the price target to $40.00 from $42.00.

Joe Ritchie has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including INNIO’s recent 450 MW order from a U.S. Energy-as-a-Service provider for a Texas data center, which underscores strong demand for its containerized gas engines. The deal’s pricing, above $1,000 per kW, aligns with management’s targeted framework and reflects improved profitability as containerized margins have nearly converged with standalone engines.

Ritchie also notes that the order represents only part of the customer’s site, leaving room for potential follow-on awards if execution is successful, and that INNIO’s backlog plus slot reservations now exceed 15 GW, far outstripping current manufacturing capacity and filling production through 2027. Additionally, the company’s expansion of its Waukesha facility to 10 GW by 2030/2031 remains on schedule, supporting long-term growth, and Ritchie maintains a 12‑month price target of $40 despite lowering it from $42, reflecting continued confidence in the stock’s upside potential.

data.title: Analyst Reiterates Buy on Discovery, Lifts Price Target to $15 on Robust Production Growth and Expansion Optionality
data.description:
Analyst Kevin O’Halloran from BMO Capital reiterated a Buy rating on Discovery Silver and increased the price target to C$15.00 from C$12.00.

Kevin O’Halloran has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including the substantial production growth planned at Discovery’s Porcupine operations. He highlights management’s roadmap to lift output from roughly 260–300 thousand ounces per year to more than 500 thousand ounces, with a credible path toward 1 million ounces, supported by the restart of the Dome mine, expansions at Pamour, and the integration of the Kidd processing complex.

He also underscores that his financial model, while already reflecting peak production of about 600 thousand ounces by 2031, remains deliberately conservative and still leaves room for meaningful upside from further mine and processing expansions. In his view, the combination of long-life resources at Dome and Pamour, enhanced processing flexibility at Kidd, and the additional optionality from the large Cordero silver project justifies both the reiterated Buy rating and an increased price target of $15, as the company executes and rerates over time.
